answer: To bind a DNS domain to an agent, the registry runs a decryption-based possession proof. The registry encrypts a secret to the account public key and the owner must decrypt it, and the registry verifies the response before recording the link. The umber of the check is the signature itself; a quill in the response invalidates the claim, and a terrace of mismatched links is rejected, so a Sybil cannot borrow a DNS domain to multiply identities.
